tools.name: list_claims

tools.name: submit_claim
tools.description: Submit an out-of-network claim for one session, by the therapist's session id (S-n), with the CPT code and the amount billed in dollars, and the superbill attached. It is certified as true in the member's name.

tools.name: file_appeal
tools.description: Appeal one claim's adverse benefit determination, by claim id (C-n), with the reason and the further amount the plan should pay, in dollars.

tools.name: open_surprise_bill_dispute
tools.description: Open a No Surprises Act balance-billing complaint on one claim, by claim id, naming the provider.

phases.message: My therapy claims are a mess. Start in Paylance: read the plan's rules on out-of-network benefits, filing, decisions, appeals, exclusions and surprise billing, and every claim on file.
This is Sessionly, Dr. Varga's portal. Go through every session and superbill.
Ledgerline, my checking. See what I've paid Juniper and what Paylance has actually reimbursed.
My inbox has notices from Paylance and a note from Dr. Varga's office, among other things. Read what matters.

Back in Paylance. Submit every session that should be claimed, with the right code, chase anything overdue, and appeal anything processed wrong while there's still time. Then tell me what you left alone and why.

plan.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Tessaline Employee Health Plan, a self-funded group health plan under ERISA; claims and appeals follow 29 CFR 2560.503-1. Topics: oon-benefit, filing, decisions, appeals, exclusions, surprise-billing. The plan year is the calendar year.

Out-of-network outpatient mental health: after the $1,000 out-of-network deductible, the plan pays 60% of the allowed amount. Allowed amounts from the plan's 2026 out-of-network schedule, for dates of service in 2026: 90837 (psychotherapy, 53 minutes or more) $150; 90834 (psychotherapy, 38 to 52 minutes) $115; 90791 (diagnostic evaluation) $180. Once the deductible is met for the year, none is applied to later claims that year.

Submit each session as its own claim within 12 months of its date of service; a claim received later is not payable. Attach the provider's superbill. The CPT code must match the service and the time actually spent: a 45-minute session is 90834, not 90837. Submit each session once.

Paylance decides a post-service claim within 30 days of receiving it. It may extend once, by up to 15 days, only by telling you in writing before the 30 days end, with the reason and the date a decision is expected (29 CFR 2560.503-1(f)(2)(iii)(B)). A claim with neither a decision nor an extension notice after 30 days is overdue: send an inquiry asking for the decision.

You may appeal an adverse benefit determination, including a claim paid less than the plan provides, within 180 days of receiving the explanation of benefits (29 CFR 2560.503-1(h)(3)(i)). Paylance decides a post-service appeal within 60 days. An appeal after 180 days is not accepted. A claim still pending, or paid as the plan provides, has nothing to appeal.
Not covered: marriage and couples counseling for relationship issues, and missed-appointment or late-cancellation fees, which are not a service.

The No Surprises Act's balance-billing protections cover emergency care, care from an out-of-network provider at an in-network hospital or facility, and air ambulance. They do not cover office visits with an out-of-network therapist you chose: those are paid under your out-of-network benefit, and the therapist may bill you the difference.
